label: churn100-s6
summary: This churn model (training AUC 0.910) is explained as six parts added on the score and passed through a sigmoid; the annotated model reproduces the original up to 5.6e-16. The strongest part is the service-call response: a gentle direct rise per call plus a gate that opens at four or more calls and that a high day charge holds shut. The 318 training customers with four or more calls churn at 50.0%, and those among them with a day charge under thirty dollars at 75.6%; switching the service-call parts off lowers the AUC to 0.808. Two usage hinges raise risk for heavy users: a high day charge without voice-mail messages (on for 1390 customers; AUC without it 0.848) and many day minutes with a high evening charge (on for 1030). The linear part is led by the international plan (0.862 per standard deviation, directly), which takes the typical customer from 1.3% to 19.7%. A per-state offset and a small state and day-charge chain complete the score.
